title: Contextual guides for migrating from tokens to components
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Problem: Designers and engineers often pick tokens directly for one-off UI pieces instead of adopting the higher-level components. Over time this causes inconsistent spacing, variant proliferation, and increased maintenance cost. Goal: Add a new set of contextual migration guides to the docs site that show when to use raw tokens versus when to adopt a component (Buttons, Tables, Charts, Controls). Each guide will include rationale, do/don't pairs, targeted code patterns, and a short migration recipe for common anti-patterns. Scope: - Top-level migration rationale page (short, persuasive). - Separate guides per surface area: tokens -> Buttons, tokens -> Table primitives -> Table component, tokens -> Chart theming -> Chart components. - 5 compact examples per guide (before/after + code + Figma link). - Accessibility callouts and testing checklist. - Quick CLI snippets for automated find/replace hints. Out of scope: full component re-implementation, breaking API changes.
acceptance_criteria: A high-level landing page exists explaining trade-offs between token-first and component-first approaches.
Three per-surface guides (Buttons, Tables, Charts) with at least five before/after examples each are published to the docs site.
Each example includes a rationale, code snippet for the current anti-pattern, the recommended component usage, and a Figma link.
An accessibility checklist is added to each guide that maps token-level concerns to component props and ARIA expectations.
Docs include a short migration recipe and one automated grep/replace example per anti-pattern.
PM and Eng sign-off on accuracy and non-breaking guidance is recorded in review comments.
steps: Audit the most common token-to-component anti-patterns from GH PRs and support tickets (design and eng owners).
Draft landing page copy and structure in Confluence; create content outline in docs repo (docs/migration/contextual-guides).
Create example implementations in the design system playground; capture Figma frames for each example.
Run internal review with PM, frontend eng, and accessibility engineer; iterate on copy and code samples.
Publish guides behind feature flag; schedule telemetry to track doc visits and links to component usage over 6 weeks.
Roll out to public docs and announce in weekly engineering sync and product newsletter.
decisions: Prefer component-first guidance for interactive controls (buttons, menus, inputs) to keep behavior and ARIA consistent.
Allow token-level usage for layout-only spacing patterns when a component cannot express the required composition.
Examples will use the stable component API (no alpha flags) so guidance applies to production teams.
Include one 'escape hatch' pattern showing how to compose a component with token overrides for rare cases.
tradeoffs: Stricter component-first guidance reduces freedom for quick prototypes but improves long-term consistency and maintenance.
Including many examples increases authoring work now but reduces recurring onboarding questions and support load.
Automatic migration hints (grep/replace) may not cover bespoke usages; we will provide manual review checklist.
technical_notes: Code examples should use the stable @redwood/ui Button props (variant, size, tone) instead of low-level token values.
Provide a small snippet for converting token-based CSS variables to component props (see docs repo snippet at tools/migrate/button-token-to-prop.sh).
Table examples will show replacing tokenized cell padding + custom sort icons with the Table component's density and icon props.
Chart theming guide will map semantic tokens (chart-accent-1) to Chart theme overrides rather than raw color variables.
